pages.transcription:

New York, 8.7.40.
Regards to all who write to me!
Dear Hanna,
I had nearly finished a letter to you announcing our
good arrival in the States when I heard that a Clipper is leaving
to-morrow so that I try to catch it still with this letter.
We have arrived yesterday afternoon after a long and
in the last days very agreable crossing, were met by Stefan's
brother, went in our old hotel, the Wyndham, had dinner with my
brother-in-law and afterwards went to see Huebsch and his wife
who are taking us to the World Fair to-night. To-day we went to
the shipping company and arranged pur departure for the 26th July
so that we would arrive in Rio on the 7th or 8th August. We in-
tend to stay in the Wyndham for a week - Stefan has only the wish
to work quietly in his room and as it is beginning to get warm and
probably soon very hot work will be the best thing to do. We do
not want to see many people and hope that the announcement of our
arrival in the papers will not lead to a number of unnecessary
or unwelcome visitors. About Eva I shall let you know as soon
as possible and we shall do our best to fix her up. In the mean-
time I hope that the arrangements in England are well under way.
We had a lot of children on board who very quickly got out of
control of their parents and made more noise than I ever expected
English children to do. - In the meantime I hope that Legintals
have moved in so that you have good company and help. I wonder
whether William is still there and who was with you all this time
and most of all whether you have had a quiet time or had to use
the old kitchen a lot. That is the worst of this distance that
such a lot of time must elapse until we hear from you. Don't for-
get to let me know how long this letter took, and when you write
tell me everything as much in detail as possible. We get a lot
of tomatoes and salad now, and that makes me think of Rosemount
each time. I hope that Manfred has been able to be with you at
least for a few days. Have you been in London in the meantime?
What about Heiner, Marta, Mama and all the others?

Kindest regards and best wishes
Lotte

Dear Hanna, we remember every moment our dear England
and follow all the news still with more eagerness than ever - as we
have not forgotten you. I have not yet all my lectures prepared
but I hope all will easily to be arranged on the way. The idea
that letters are taking still more time from South America is
very oppressive as we would like to hear every day from you and
to have your news as fresh as our eggs at Rosemount. Please tell
Eidemann that he may do after his own choice and go also farther
than I thought first, give him and everybody my best regards
Stefan Zweig

[Randnotiz links:] A big photograph of Lotte was in the
newspapers with my own.
